paper_id: Shangguan et al. - 2013 - OTrack Order tracking for luggage in mobile RFID systems
title: OTrack: Order Tracking for Luggage in Mobile RFID Systems
motivation: Manual luggage processing incurs loss and tremendous financial damage; existing RFID systems cannot track tag order on conveyor belts
problem_framing: Infer relative positions of tags on moving belt from communication attributes without direct localization
key_insight: Combination of RRR critical region and RSSI peak within it yields stable temporal reference; single attributes fail but their intelligent combination works
method_signature: RRR-variance-based critical region detection + RSSI quadratic fitting + insertion sorting
evaluation_criteria: Accuracy Ratio = correctly ordered tags / total shipped tags
negative_result_or_admitted_limitation: FCFS achieves only 55% accuracy; G-RSSI fails due to RSSI fluctuation; existing localization methods require complex deployment and cause significant error
evidence_for_taste: only 55% of luggage has been ordered correctly
G-RSSI fails to directly capture the order of tags
The critical region actually indicates that the tag is of good SNR
neither of the order of tag identification nor the RSSI provides sufficient evidence
such a region always exists in the RRR trace of each tag
thinking_moves: 从单独属性失败反推需要属性组合
从物理直觉(距离近→信号好)提炼出critical region概念
用概率论(中心极限定理)严格化启发式观察
先验证各基线方法都失败,再提出组合方案
